lessons: CRITICAL FIX: the cash-use law scope was too narrow AND missing its second limb. The skill said the 6,000 NIS cap applies 'in a business-to-business transaction'. Verified against חוק לצמצום השימוש במזומן: section 2(א) binds a dealer giving OR receiving, and section 2(ג) binds a non-dealer paying a dealer, so the cap applies whenever a dealer is a party. The 15,000 figure applies only where NEITHER side is a dealer. Separately, permitted cash is the LOWER of the scheduled amount or 10% of the transaction price ('למעט סכום הנמוך מבין... 10% ממחיר העסקה'), so on a 20,000 NIS deal the real ceiling is 2,000. Under the same Circular 3/2026 the skill cites, a cash-law breach is what disallows the deduction, so getting this wrong costs the user the expense.

CRITICAL FIX: Form 102 for INCOME-TAX deductions is due the 16th, not the 15th. The 15th is the Bituach Leumi date, and BTL has its own separate form also called 102. The ITA's annual deadline announcement is explicit: 'ב-15 לכל חודש, חל מועד הדיווח והתשלום לדוחות התקופתיים למע"מ ולמקדמות מס הכנסה' versus 'ב-16 לכל חודש, חל מועד הדיווח ותשלום לניכויים למס-הכנסה'. I flagged this as unverifiable during the research pass and deliberately left it alone; the review pass resolved it.

STALE FIGURE FIXED: the de-minimis threshold was 4,920-5,040 (the 2015 and 2022 values). It is 5,520 for 2024-2026, verified verbatim in the Nevo text: 'הוראות סעיף זה לא יחולו על עסקה שמחירה אינו עולה על 5,520 שקלים חדשים שהתקשר בה גוף ציבורי'. The citation chain is regulation 2 of the 1977 withholding regs incorporating section 2(ב) of חוק עסקאות גופים ציבוריים.

REMOVED an unsourced qualifier: the skill described the de-minimis as VAT-inclusive. Neither the 1977 regulation ('ששוויים') nor the public-bodies law ('שמחירה') says so. The question is genuinely open in the primary text, so it is now asserted neither way.

CORRECTED the royalties row. The 1977 regulations create no separate royalties category: a payment to an Israeli resident falls under the 20%/30% services-and-assets default, and a payment to a non-resident is withheld under section 170. The reviewer rightly warned that the first wording tipped into implying 23% is not a real rate at all, so the calculator constant was kept and annotated rather than deleted.
CORRECTED 'substantial shareholder' from 'over 10%' to '10% or more' (section 88).

ADDED the TY2025 filing extension: the ITA extended the Form 126 and 856 deadline to 31 May 2026, with reports transmitted and approved online through 30 June 2026 treated as timely. Extensions like this are announced most years, so the skill now tells the agent to check the current year before telling a user they are late.

TREATY TABLE REFRESHED on three stale rows. UK royalties are 0% under the 2019 Protocol in force for amounts paid from 1.1.2020 (the table said 15%); Germany updated to the treaty effective 1.1.2017; Canada updated to the convention in force 21.12.2016 with the 5% dividend tier at a 25% holding, not 10%.

PROCESS, fifth occurrence in this batch: the first pass corrected the de-minimis and the cash-law scope in the SKILL files but left BOTH stale in evidence.json, which then actively contradicted the corrected body, and left 'including VAT' standing in the reference file that the skill tells the agent to consult for the default rate. The rule that keeps working: after any change, grep the OLD value across the WHOLE folder including evidence.json, metadata.json and scripts, and require zero hits before running the panel.

CARRY: non-resident withholding under section 170 is not a flat 25%. It is 25% where the payee is an individual and the corporate rate where the payee is a company. The prose now hedges to 'commonly applied at 25%' but the calculator still hardcodes non_resident = 0.25 with no company branch.

CARRY: the Circular 3/2026 description overstates two things. Input-VAT denial sits on the allocation-number and cash-law tracks, not on the withholding-failure track (which is section 32א, income-tax expense disallowance only). And the package is staggered: the cash-law limb runs from 1.1.2026 but the allocation-number limb runs from 1.8.2025.

CARRY: 'treaty relief needs prior approval from the assessing officer' is stated absolutely. Since 2017 a green-track bank-declaration route exists for a narrow set of enumerated capital transactions. The practical advice survives for service and royalty payments, but the absolute framing over-sends users to the assessing officer.

CARRY: calculator drift. --type royalties returns 0.23 even for a resident payee, where the prose now says 20%/30% applies. The --rates section labels attribute section 170 to everything not explicitly 164, so services_with_books, rent_residential and contractor print as 170 when rent has its own 1998 regulations.

CARRY: the USA and France treaty rows are incomplete rather than wrong (USA omits the 10% interest and 10% royalty tiers and the 15% dividend tier; France omits the 5% dividend, 5% interest and 0% royalty tiers).
